name: N-acetylcysteine (NAC)
mechanism: Replenishes glutathione to detoxify NAPQI in paracetamol overdose
dosing: Intravenous regimens commonly used: e.g., 150 mg/kg over 1 hour, then 50 mg/kg over 4 hours, then 100 mg/kg over 16 hours (weight-adjusted); oral 72-hour protocol also used—follow local toxicology protocol
contraindications: Known hypersensitivity to NAC or formulation components; caution in asthmatic patients due to bronchospasm risk
interactions: May interact with activated charcoal if given orally (adsorption) — coordinate timing; otherwise few clinically significant drug interactions when used as antidote
monitoring: Monitor LFTs, renal function and clinical status; observe for anaphylactoid or allergic-type reactions during IV infusion and manage accordingly; monitor paracetamol concentration to guide treatment duration
pregnancy: Use when indicated for paracetamol overdose; benefits of antidote outweigh risks
sideEffects: Anaphylactoid reactions during rapid IV infusion (flushing, bronchospasm, hypotension); gastrointestinal upset with oral regimen
clinicalPearls: Start NAC empirically if there is uncertainty about timing of significant paracetamol ingestion and levels are not available; consult toxicology and follow local protocols
indication: Antidote for paracetamol (acetaminophen) overdose; mucolytic use separate and lower-dose when indicated
